_openQuestions: STATUS — Akis confirmed on 2026-08-25 that bina is live in all five states: Arizona, Idaho, Utah, Wyoming and New Hampshire. esa-states.json was updated to match (Wyoming and New Hampshire moved from coming-soon to approved). Two places still lag and are not this page's to fix: the upstream bina-gtm/notes/ESA_State_Database.xlsx, and thebinaschool.com's homepage, which still names only Utah, Arizona and Wyoming.

thebinaschool.com says ESA funding 'covers tuition in full' for Utah, Arizona and Wyoming. It does not: the largest base award in those states is $8,000 against $10,769 yearly tuition. These pages publish the remainder instead. The homepage line should be corrected.

Application windows: only Arizona and New Hampshire take applications year-round. Utah's 2026-27 window closed (next opens spring), Idaho's second 2026 window closed 2026-08-15, Wyoming's closed end of July. The closed-window pages sell the school now and line the family up for the next window — that is deliberate, and it is why paid budget should weight Arizona.

Class size: the main site says 'never more than 12 in a class'; /esa already publishes 'small live classes of 6-8 with two teachers'; the Google Ads copy says 'typical class size 7-8 kids'. These pages publish 6-8 with two teachers, capped at 12 — the union of what we already say. Confirm with the CSO.
The $8,000 (Utah) / $7,000-$8,000 (Arizona) figures are base awards. Children with special needs qualify for more in several states; the pages say so without quoting an amount.

faq.q: Is bina a homeschool program or a school?
faq.a: A school. Your child has a class, a timetable, certified teachers and report cards — the same structure as an in-person school, delivered live online. Most state programs list us under online or nonpublic schooling rather than homeschool curriculum, and we tell you exactly which category applies in your state before you apply.

faq.q: What if my state approves me for less than the full amount?
faq.a: You pay the difference. We show you the number before you commit, and we offer quarterly and yearly plans plus $1,500 off per additional child, so the gap is a monthly figure you can plan around.

faq.q: What if my application is turned down, or the window has closed?
faq.a: You are not stuck with a school you never chose. Families join bina and pay directly while an application is pending, and we time your start around your funding date once it is confirmed. Nothing about enrolling forces you to wait for the state.

faq.q: My child is neurodivergent or has an IEP. Does that change anything?
faq.a: Often in your favour — several states fund more per child for special needs. On our side, small classes and a Family Success team are the whole point; parents of neurodivergent children are a large share of our families, and they say so in the reviews on this page.

faq.q: Can I use ESA money for bina alongside other things?
faq.a: That depends on your state's rules and your award, not on us. Tuition for an online school is an approved category in the states listed here; whether there is room left over for other purchases is a question for your state's handbook, and we will point you at the exact page.

faq.q: We live in a state that isn't listed. Can we still join?
faq.a: Yes — families join bina from all over the world without any state funding. And new programs are approved most years: our state-by-state ESA tool shows where every US state stands today, including the states with no program at all.
